messages:
Maya Patel: quick follow-up from today's all-hands q&a thread 1: collecting the process items so we can publish a short FAQ and example playbooks.

Diego Alvarez: two asks from my team: 1) are we settling on a single release cadence across the org? 2) what concrete perf gates should block a rollout for runtime changes?

Lena Brooks: TL;DR from leadership: were standardizing on a default cadence of biweekly for product feature releases; infra/runtime keeps weekly cycles for small patches or uses staged 3-step rollouts for higher-risk infra changes. weekly canaries remain available for fast feedback.

Lena Brooks: perf gate specifics: metric set = {latency_p95, latency_p99, qps, memory_rss}. if latency_p95 regresses >10% or memory_rss increases >15% for the same load profile, the change must block the release until mitigated. include bench links in PRs.

Ravi Patel: oncall follow-up: primary rotation = 1 week, backup = 2 weeks. we're testing a single handoff message in #eng-oncall every Monday 09:00 PT to reduce duplicate posts. runbook updates required after each handoff.

Diego Alvarez: SLA customer question: what latency numbers do we advertise for Dedicated customers and do we automatically failover to alternate regions/models?

Lena Brooks: Dedicated: uptime SLA 99.9% plus contract-level p95 targets. example guidance well publish: small-seq p95 ~<=200ms, long-context p95 <=500-600ms depending on model. automatic fallback chains (model_variant -> region -> degraded_variant) are enabled for critical routes by default; customers see this behavior in the incident FAQ.

Maya Patel: can someone produce a compact PR template snippet to enforce perf bench artifacts and rollout notes? leadership wants that in the PR process by next week.

Ravi Patel: draft PR template snippet below (suggest edits):
```
PR checklist:
- unit & integration tests updated
- bench run attached (link) showing p95/p99/qps/memory for baseline and branch
- perf diff <10% p95, <15% memory (otherwise block)
- canary + rollback plan documented
- security review if applicable
```

OpsBot: scheduled canary lane created by @Lena Brooks for release/1829 (24h window).

Diego Alvarez: thanks. final ask: can eng-sre publish exact metric ids and a small bench script so product teams can automate perf comparisons?

Ravi Patel: will post metric ids (latency_p95, latency_p99, qps, memory_rss) and a minimal bench script in #eng-sre by EOD tomorrow.

Maya Patel: i'll run a 30-min office hours tomorrow 11:00 PT to walk through examples (when to choose weekly canary vs biweekly release), review the PR checklist, and confirm oncall handoff changes. will publish notes and action items after. please keep replies short here so we can fold them into the doc. :thumbsup:
